factor_name: Innovative efficiency based on patents granted scaled by R&D capital (EMI1)
economic_intuition: Firms that generate more patents per dollar of R&D investment are more innovatively efficient; investors may underreact to this less-salient information, producing higher subsequent returns.
detailed_definition: Patents granted in year y scaled by five-year cumulative R&D expenses ending in fiscal years y-2 through y-6 with 20% annual depreciation weights.

source_details: market equity at the end of June
U.S. patents granted by the USPTO

evidence.quote: two-year gap between R&D capital and patents
evidence.interpretation: The formula and lag structure are stated in the paper and linked to the patent application-grant lag.

evidence.quote: IE measures in year t – 1 are fully observable
evidence.interpretation: The EMI factor forms portfolios at the end of June t using IE from year t-1; this is a June formation delay rather than an explicit accounting lag for the EMI factor.
The paper explicitly sets missing R&D to zero in denominator calculations, but does not otherwise state a global missing-data imputation rule.
